title: 0. Executive Thesis, Dual Verdict & Opportunity Matrix

epigraph.quote: When an unexplained volume spike pushes a cyclical developer above risk-adjusted fair value, judge every rupee on forward opportunity cost: reject new capital, cut half of existing holdings, and tighten the stop beneath the 10-week EMA.
epigraph.author: Executive Investment Committee

web_blocks.html: Executive Thesis (November 2026 Refresh): Ajmera Realty (NSE: AJMERA) is a 58-year-old Mumbai developer [2][8]. Its balance sheet rests on a near-zero-cost 100-acre Wadala i-Land township and 68.56% promoter ownership (0.02% pledge) [8][43]. Between FY21 and FY26, revenue tripled to ₹1,090 crore (₹1,247 crore TTM) and net profit rose 5.1x to ₹157 crore (₹180 crore TTM) [8]. On-book debt fell ₹34 crore in Q2 FY27 to ₹646 crore (0.44x D/E), keeping its Crisil A-/Stable rating [32][33]. Yet we maintain CYCLICAL_CONDITIONAL (kpi_health: PASS_WITH_WATCH). Pass 1 forensics flagged 53% twelve-year CFO/PAT, 82% receivables coverage (down from 100%), and ₹1,465 crore in planned debt alongside a ₹500 crore NCD resolution [8][32][38]. Contingent liabilities jumped 60x to ₹456.89 crore (~₹22.90/share, 31% of net worth), joined by a ₹125 crore associate guarantee and a qualified Bahrain audit [35][36][37]. Inside Wadala East, Dosti Eastern Bay and Raymond Realty create a pricing pincer ahead of an 86% H2 FY27 pre-sales hurdle (₹307 crore H1 vs. ₹2,200 crore target) [14][40][41].

Dual Verdict (Derived from Chapter 9): AJMERA surged to ₹162.62 on the 2026-11-23 NSE ledger (+8.93% on 28.44x volume; Stage 2 Markup) [27]. On the 2026-11-25 live TradingView tape, it trades at ₹160.92 (18.72x P/E, 2.16x P/B, in_thewrap_stage2: True, RS 82.1) [26]. On November 24, management filed a voluntary Reg 30 note confirming zero undisclosed news [34]. Price sits +18.25% above its 10W EMA (₹136.09) and +26.90% above its 50D SMA (₹126.81), with Daily RSI at 76.31 and 4H RSI at 78.69 [26]. Deducting ₹22.90/share for ₹456.89 crore contingencies from ₹171.00 gross SOTP NAV yields a ₹148.00 Base target (15.6x FY28E EPS ₹9.46). Probability-weighted E[P] sits at ₹149.00 (-7.4% vs. ₹160.92). New capital is therefore REJECTED (TIER_0; VALUATION, CASH_FLOW). Because AJMERA has no NSE options chain (NOT_OPTIONABLE_OR_ILLIQUID), we act in cash equity [28]. On forward opportunity cost, we TRIM_INTO_STRENGTH on our 1,300 Zerodha shares (4.96% NAV at ₹162.62 ledger; ₹209,196 live at ₹160.92) [26][29]. Sell 650 shares (50%) (~₹1,04,598 cash) and ratchet the weekly stop up from ₹117.00 to ₹134.00 on 650 shares (~2.45% NAV).

web_blocks.title: Dossier Refresh Architecture & Dual-Cutoff Clarity
paragraphs: Chapters 1–6 remain price-blind fundamental audits patched with Pass 1 blind spots. Chapter 4 maps the Wadala East pricing pincer. Chapter 6 adds CRISIL's 82% receivables coverage, ₹1,465 Cr planned debt, ₹456.89 Cr contingencies, the ₹125 Cr associate guarantee, and the Bahrain audit qualification. Chapters 7–9 layer the explicit SOTP contingency bridge (Ch 7), the extended Stage 2 tape and Nov 24 no-UPSI spike (Ch 8), and our executable 50% trim and ₹134.00 stop-ratchet plan (Ch 9). Throughout, 2026-11-23 NSE ledger closes (₹162.62) are clearly separated from 2026-11-25 live TradingView closes (₹160.92).

book_paragraphs: Welcome to the November 2026 refreshed institutional research dossier on Ajmera Realty & Infra India Limited. Before we walk through the fifty-eight-year history of the Ajmera family, the economics of their 100-acre Wadala township, and our newly patched balance-sheet and micro-market forensics, let us put the updated executive thesis and dual portfolio verdict right on the table.

At its core, Ajmera Realty remains a cyclical Mumbai asset-conversion story backed by a genuine legacy land bank. Its near-zero-cost Wadala i-Land township helped triple consolidated revenue from ₹347 crore in FY21 to ₹1,090 crore in FY26 (₹1,247 crore trailing) and expand net profit more than fivefold to ₹157 crore (₹180 crore trailing), while Q2 FY27 on-book debt dipped ₹34 crore to ₹646 crore (0.44x D/E) with a reaffirmed Crisil A-/Stable rating. Yet our Pass 1 refresh kept business quality at CYCLICAL_CONDITIONAL (PASS_WITH_WATCH) after surfacing material unpriced risks: twelve-year CFO-to-PAT sits at just 53%, committed receivables coverage stepped down from 100% to 82%, CRISIL models ₹1,465 crore of planned incremental project debt alongside a ₹500 crore NCD enabling approval, FY26 contingent liabilities surged 60-fold to ₹456.89 crore (~₹22.90 per share, 31% of net worth) alongside a ₹125 crore associate corporate guarantee, the 60% Bahrain subsidiary carries a qualified FY26 audit, and a Wadala East supply wall from unlisted Dosti Eastern Bay and Raymond Realty caps pricing power.

Against that heavier risk ledger, the share price erupted vertically. On the verified November 23 NSE ledger, Ajmera spiked 8.93% to ₹162.62 on an extraordinary 28.44 times its 20-day average volume—prompting a voluntary November 24 Regulation 30 clarification confirming zero undisclosed price-sensitive information. On the November 25 live TradingView snapshot, shares stand at ₹160.92 (18.72x trailing P/E, 2.16x book value), stretched +18.25% above the 10-week EMA (₹136.09) and +26.90% above the 50-day SMA (₹126.81) with daily RSI at 76.31 and 4-hour RSI at 78.69. Once we deduct ₹22.90 per share for contingent liabilities from our ₹171.00 gross SOTP NAV, Base fair value drops to ₹148.00 (15.6x FY28E EPS ₹9.46) and probability-weighted expected value sits at ₹149.00 (-7.4% vs. ₹160.92). New capital is therefore strictly REJECTED (TIER_0; VALUATION, CASH_FLOW).

For our existing Zerodha stake of 1,300 shares—worth ₹211,406.00 (4.96% weight) at the ₹162.62 ledger close and ₹209,196.00 live at ₹160.92—evaluating strictly on forward mark-to-market opportunity cost dictates TRIM_INTO_STRENGTH. Sell 650 shares (50%) immediately to harvest ~₹1,04,598 cash, halve exposure to ~2.45% NAV, and ratchet the hard weekly-close stop upward from ₹117.00 to ₹134.00 (just below the rising 10-week EMA) on the remaining 650 shares.

book_callouts.text: New capital is REJECTED (TIER_0; VALUATION, CASH_FLOW). On forward opportunity cost, TRIM_INTO_STRENGTH by selling 650 of 1,300 held shares (50%) near ₹160.92 and ratcheting the weekly stop up from ₹117.00 to ₹134.00.

book_subsections.title: What Changed Since Mid-November—and Why We Cut Exposure in Half
paragraphs: Two shifts drive our November 25 refresh. First, on the tape, Ajmera jumped more than 18% in a single week from ₹135.69 to ₹160.92 (₹162.62 on the November 23 ledger) on a 28.44x volume explosion, compressing its P/E discount to mid-cap peer Sunteck Realty to just 10.4% and pushing its book multiple to 2.16x—even though management confirmed on November 24 that no undisclosed corporate event drove the move.

Second, in the footnotes, Pass 1 uncovered that CRISIL's August 4, 2026 rationale cut committed receivables coverage from 100% to 82% and flagged ₹1,465 crore in planned incremental project debt, while FY26 consolidated contingent liabilities climbed to ₹456.89 crore (~₹22.90 per share, 31% of net worth) and Wadala East competition intensified from Dosti Realty and Raymond Realty. Deducting those contingencies drops Base fair value to ₹148.00 (-8.0% vs. ₹160.92), making a 50% trim and a tightened ₹134.00 stop the cleanest forward risk decision.

book_subsections.title: How to Navigate This Ten-Chapter Refreshed Monograph
paragraphs: As always, we keep fundamental research strictly separated from market price. Chapters 1 through 6 audit Ajmera's fifty-eight-year corporate history, Wadala/MMR/Bengaluru segments, Mivan construction and channel unit economics, competitive moat—now updated with the Wadala East supply pincer—management's H2 FY27 pre-sales hurdle, and twelve-year financial forensics, now updated with off-balance-sheet contingencies, associate guarantees, planned incremental debt, and the Bahrain subsidiary audit qualification.

Chapters 7 through 9 then bring in the live November 23 ledger and November 25 TradingView tape. Chapter 7 runs the updated five-peer comparison, Reverse DCF, and explicit SOTP contingency-haircut bridge (₹171.00 less ₹22.90/share = ₹148.00). Chapter 8 dissects the Stage 2 breakout, the +26.90% 50-day SMA extension, the November 24 no-UPSI filing, and our tightened stop-loss ratchet to ₹134.00. Chapter 9 synthesizes the Steelman Bull and Bear cases, the ₹149.00 expected value, and the exact execution rules for our 50% Zerodha trim and 50/50 Cash/TITAN redeployment.

book_subsections.title: Opportunity Cost: Rotating ₹1,04,598 of Trim Proceeds Into Quality at Support
paragraphs: Selling 650 shares of an extended cyclical developer is only half the trade; the other half is deploying that capital where forward risk-reward is genuinely asymmetric. With our Zerodha account already holding ₹1,420,949.94 in cash (33.3% of ₹4,264,304.99 net worth) inside a narrow-breadth Nifty 50 uptrend (55.2% of stocks above 50DMA, three distribution days), we keep 50% of our ~₹1,04,598 trim proceeds and next marginal ₹100,000 in liquid cash.

The remaining 50% routes directly to active shortlist compounder TITAN, trading at ₹4,686.60 on the November 25 live TradingView tape (STAGE_2, +0.15% above its 10-week EMA at ₹4,679.69, RSI 48.77, vs. ₹4,680.00 Stage 3 on the November 23 ledger)—right inside its ₹4,550.00–₹4,696.38 support band with a ₹4,380.00 stop, ₹5,600.00 Base target, 2.86:1 asymmetry, and 45.28% ROE. Meanwhile, we keep Oberoi Realty at 0% so we never double Mumbai real-estate beta alongside our remaining 650 Ajmera shares.

book_subsections.title: Four Anchor Numbers to Keep in Mind
paragraphs: Carry four verified anchor figures as you read or listen through the monograph. First, the 2026-11-23 NSE ledger close is ₹162.62 (28.44x volume) and the 2026-11-25 live TradingView snapshot is ₹160.92, valuing Ajmera at ₹3,207.77 crore (18.72x TTM P/E, 2.16x P/B). Second, we trim 650 of our 1,300 held Zerodha shares (50%, harvesting ~₹1,04,598 cash) and ratchet the hard weekly-close stop up from ₹117.00 to ₹134.00 on the remaining 650 shares (~2.45% NAV, capping forward risk at -16.7%). Third, our 12-month targets stand at ₹105.00 Bear (25%), ₹148.00 Base (50%; 15.6x FY28E EPS ₹9.46), and ₹195.00 Bull (25%), yielding a ₹149.00 probability-weighted fair value (-7.4% vs. ₹160.92). Fourth, new capital is strictly REJECTED (TIER_0; VALUATION, CASH_FLOW).

With those guardrails locked, let us begin in Chapter 1—tracing how a fifty-eight-year family construction enterprise built one of Mumbai's most valuable legacy land banks and navigated five decades of real estate cycles.
